signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Middle East Escalation
signals.text: NOK 1W average gain of +1.677% (n=2) versus EUR 1W decline of -1.020% (n=9) establishes a 2.697% G10 spread that anchors upside pressure into the open. Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks and Brent testing $120 amplify terms-of-trade divergence between energy-exporting Norway and import-dependent Europe, compound by French 10Y yields breaking above 5.0%. The Sydney open and subsequent European cash open serve as the resolution window for this divergence. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/EUR into the session open shaped by crude supply disruption premia. Catalyst: Monday European cash open and Germany Ifo survey releases. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Persian Gulf or Brent falling sharply back below $110.

signals.title: EUR/USD — French Debt Strain + Crowded Leveraged Shorts
signals.text: EUR COT leveraged funds net short sits at -94,138 contracts (33.6% long, 2nd percentile 52-week) creating positioning stretch, but French 10-year yields topping 5% and sovereign debt strain keep spot capped below its falling 20-day SMA at 1.1238. Transatlantic carry firmly favors the dollar with Fed SOFR at 3.90% against ECB €STR at 2.44% (+146bp spread), which restricts recovery attempts despite BEER model valuation showing EUR/USD cheap at -2.62σ. The ECB policy meeting on 29 Oct and Fed decision on 28 Oct determine the medium-term path, preceded immediately by Germany Ifo data. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD below the 1.1238 20-day SMA. Catalyst: German Ifo Business Climate release at 09:30 UTC followed by the ECB meeting on 29 Oct. Risk: Upside breach of 1.1240 triggering short covering from stretched -94.1k leveraged fund shorts.
evidence: OIS carry: +146bp in favor of USD

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction

signals.title: USD/CAD — Tariff Relief + BoC Policy Divergence
signals.text: CAD COT leveraged funds net short stands at -92,789 contracts (17.6% long, 12th percentile 52-week), leaving the pair exposed to a sharp downside squeeze following reports the US will lift 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. Spot closed Friday at 1.4004 below its 1.4009 50-day SMA, breaking the 10-day closing low as markets price Bank of Canada hike risks against an expected Federal Reserve pause. The Bank of Canada policy rate decision on 28 Oct is the catalyst that validates or rejects the policy wedge against Fed SOFR's 165bp carry advantage. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD on tariff relief momentum and short-covering. Catalyst: Bank of Canada policy meeting on 28 Oct alongside the Fed decision on 28 Oct. Risk: BoC holds rates at 2.25% with dovish forward guidance, restoring USD yield dominance above 1.4050.
evidence: Reported US removal of 50% Canadian tariffs

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Safe-Haven Bid vs Carry Advantage
signals.text: Middle East military tensions and naval mine strikes near the Strait of Hormuz drive defensive demand for JPY, pressing spot to close Friday at 156.81 below its 20-day SMA of 157.87. However, the 267bp OIS yield advantage favoring USD (SOFR 3.90% vs TONA 1.23%) and leveraged fund JPY net shorts of -25,598 contracts limit sustained yen follow-through unless 156.00 breaks. The Bank of Japan policy decision on 30 Oct is the catalyst for whether Japanese yields adjust upward to narrow the 220bp 10-year sovereign spread. Trade bias: Neutral-to-bearish USD/JPY targeting 156.00 while capped under 157.50. Catalyst: Tokyo market open followed by the BoJ policy meeting on 30 Oct. Risk: Headline de-escalation in the Middle East driving immediate carry rebuilding toward 158.00.
evidence: OIS carry: +267bp in favor of USD

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning vs Domestic Data Softness
signals.text: AUD COT leveraged funds net long at +47,606 contracts (69.3% long) establishes crowded long exposure after Friday's close at 0.7038 into descending 200-day SMA resistance at 0.7052. Although RBA hike pricing and an AONIA-over-SOFR carry premium of +70bp support spot, Australia's Economic Surprise Index at -5.7 and an unemployment rate spike to 4.7% (z=+4.04σ shock) erode underlying domestic macro support. The Reserve Bank of Australia meeting on 3 Nov is the definitive test for whether cash rate expectations sustain spot above 0.7000. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD with downside bias on any break below 0.6980. Catalyst: Sydney session open and RBA meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: Broad US dollar weakness pushing AUD/USD through the 0.7052 200-day SMA.
